newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares hover above 1997 lows. [CORRECTED 21:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares hover above 1997 lows. [CORRECTED 21:52 GMT]

text.p: Jordanian shares hovered just above 1997 lows on Wednesday, propped up by healthy profits in two industrial firms and upward corrections in other industry stocks, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.01 points to close the week on 151.64 points, barely above a 1997 low of 151.61 points at the start of January.
"It's stable. People are in wait-and-see mode," said analyst Mohammad Abdullah of Pearl Consulting.

Wednesday's fractional rise, on modest turnover of 433,000 dinars ($612,000), ended four days of consecutive falls prompted by a number of shares going ex-dividend and disappointing results from smaller industrial firms.
But Abdallah said strong results on Wednesday from Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturers (Corrects) and Jordan Electric Power reassured the market.
He said Arab Pharmaceutical, helped by a sharp cut in corporate tax last year, doubled its net profit to 3.39 million dinars from 1.69 million in 1995.
The stock closed unchanged at 3.72 dinars (Corrects). The company is expected to benefit in 1997 from increased sales to Iraq under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

Jordan Electric Power, which rose sharply earlier in the week on expectation of good results, did not disappoint. Its shares were steady at 1.69 dinars on turnover worth 39,000 dinars after it announced profits up 36 percent at 3.18 million dinars.

Other food and industrial firms, including Jordan Rock Wool Industries and Univeral Modern Industries which tumbled around 10 percent earlier in the week after announcing poor results, rose on Wednesday.
"Today there was a correction. They had fallen five percent for two days but that was a shock reaction," Abdallah said.
Busiest stock of the day was Arab Potash Company, which has yet to announced its full 1997 results. Shares worth 111,000 dinars were traded but the stock closed unchanged on 6.10 dinars.
Overall 19 shares rose, 15 fell and another 11 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.12 percent to 79.58 points, still 4.57 percent down from the start of the year.
